applies_why: The judge text resolves a disputed link by saying the cited texts do not state the contrary in their own words, which is the kind of verse-level stating-verse test K-C governs.
quote: D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires': I read it either as forbidding the judge to require an own-words contrary before finding a link supported, or as permitting a mere underdetermination finding where no text states a verdict; the former controls because the judge expressly decides UNDERDETERMINED on the absence of contrary own words.
why: The judge calls the link underdetermined because neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain weighing by footing.
